title: Mining Point-of-No-Return Boundaries in Constrained Dynamical Systems via Counterfactual Auditing

problem.claim: Safety-critical failures in constrained dynamical environments are often detected only after violation, and outcome metrics conflate structural inevitability with decision-induced errors.

gap.claim: Existing outcome metrics do not separate structurally inevitable failures from errors induced by decisions.

contributions.claim: The paper formulates failure diagnosis as recoverability boundary discovery and defines the Point-of-No-Return as the last recoverable snapshot before violation becomes unavoidable under an audited intervention class.
Counterfactual PoNR Auditing is a snapshot-replay framework that produces matched counterfactual rollouts and uses a neural operator surrogate for acceleration.
The framework produces Evidence Objects for structural-policy decomposition, supports Failure Atlas mining, and can generate offline supervision for lightweight predictors.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The neural operator surrogate provides a reported 3.09× end-to-end speedup.
Experiments on a high-fidelity hydrodynamic control testbed and a canonical bistable system reportedly show that PoNR precedes observable violation.
The reported experiments show stability under up to 30% multiplicative surrogate noise and reduced auditing cost through surrogate-guided search.

narrative_sequence.summary: Safety-critical failures are detected too late, while outcome metrics mix structural inevitability with decision-induced error.
Failure diagnosis is reframed as discovery of the last recoverable snapshot before unavoidable violation.
Counterfactual PoNR Auditing replays snapshots, generates matched counterfactual rollouts, and uses a neural operator surrogate for speed.
Evidence Objects enable structural-policy decomposition and Failure Atlas mining through contrastive event-sequence analysis.
Experiments report early PoNR detection, noise stability, and lower auditing cost across two dynamical-system settings.

source_observation.claim: The method defines a boundary using counterfactual recoverability rather than waiting for an observed violation.

interpretation.claim: Counterfactual analysis can distinguish failures that were already structurally unavoidable from failures caused by intervenable decisions.

application.claim: For safety-critical sequential systems, audit snapshots near suspected failure points with matched interventions and preserve evidence objects for structural-policy attribution.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish applicability beyond constrained dynamical systems or beyond the specified audited intervention class.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the audited intervention class in detail.
The abstract does not describe the counterfactual rollout algorithm or surrogate architecture.
The abstract does not report quantitative baselines, dataset sizes, or statistical uncertainty.
